chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Maḥfūẓ al-Iskāf, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

When you wish to bury the deceased, let the most intelligent of those who descend into his grave be at his head. Let him uncover his right cheek until he places it upon the earth, bring his mouth close to his hearing, and say: 'Listen and understand' three times: 'Allah is your Lord, Muḥammad is your Prophet, Islam is your religion, and so-and-so is your Imam.' 'Listen and understand'—and repeat it to him three times. This is the talqīn.

key_terms.إِمَامُكَ: your Imam, whose name is to be specified for the deceased
key_terms.اسْمَعْ وَافْهَمْ: an instruction to listen and understand, repeated in talqīn
key_terms.نَبِيُّكَ: your Prophet, referring to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What should be said to the deceased during burial in the Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of talqīn at the time of burial, instructing that the deceased be reminded of the foundational truths of faith. It presents a funerary rite centered on affirming Lordship, prophethood, religion, and Imamate as the deceased is placed in the grave.
